translation_en: Ibn Abbas reported that his maternal aunt, Umm Hufayd bint al-Harith, gave the Prophet ghee, dried curds, and desert lizards. He called for them, and they were eaten at his table. He left the lizards uneaten, as though he disliked them. Ibn Abbas said that if they had been unlawful, they would not have been eaten at the Prophet's table, nor would he have ordered people to eat them.

Suwayd bin al-Numan reported that they were with the Prophet at al-Sahba, about an afternoon's journey from Khaybar, when prayer time came. He asked for food, but only roasted barley flour mixed with water was available. He chewed some, and they chewed and ate with him. Then he asked for water, rinsed his mouth, and prayed, and they prayed with him, without performing ablution.

Khalid bin al-Walid reported that he entered with the Messenger of Allah upon Maymunah, who was his aunt and Ibn Abbas's aunt. They found roasted desert lizard there, brought by her sister Hufaydah from Najd. She offered it to the Messenger, who rarely reached for food until he had been told what it was. When one of the women told him it was lizard, he withdrew his hand. Khalid asked whether it was unlawful. He said, No, but it is not found in my people's land, so I find myself disinclined to eat it. Khalid pulled it toward himself and ate while the Messenger watched. This report was conveyed by Ibn Abbas from Khalid, who was known as the Sword of Allah. Maymunah was Khalid's aunt as well as Ibn Abbas's. Her sister Hufaydah had brought the lizard from Najd. The Prophet customarily waited to be told what food was before eating it.

Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah said, Food for two is enough for three, and food for three is enough for four. The Messenger of Allah taught that a modest amount of food can suffice for more people when they share it. The report was narrated by Abu Huraira.

Nafi reported that Ibn Umar would not eat until a poor person was brought to eat with him. Nafi once brought in a man, who ate a great deal. Ibn Umar said, Nafi, do not bring this man to me. I heard the Prophet say, The believer eats in one intestine, while the disbeliever eats in seven intestines.

Ibn Umar reported that the Messenger of Allah said, The believer eats in one intestine, while the disbeliever—or the hypocrite, for Ubaidullah was unsure which word was used—eats in seven intestines. Ibn Bukayr also reported the same wording from Malik, from Nafi, from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet.

Amr reported that Abu Nuhayk was a man who ate a great deal. Ibn Umar told him, The Messenger of Allah said, The disbeliever eats in seven intestines. Abu Nuhayk replied, I believe in Allah and His Messenger.

Abu Huraira reported that the Messenger of Allah said, A Muslim eats in one intestine, while a disbeliever eats in seven intestines. This wording was narrated by Abu Huraira from the Messenger of Allah. It appears among reports about the believer's and disbeliever's eating.

Abu Huraira reported that a man used to eat a great deal, but after he became Muslim he ate little. This was mentioned to the Prophet, who said, The believer eats in one intestine, while the disbeliever eats in seven intestines.
Abu Juhaifa reported that the Messenger of Allah said, I do not eat while reclining. Abu Juhaifa heard this statement directly from the Messenger of Allah.

Abu Juhaifa said he was with the Prophet when he told a man who was there, I do not eat while reclining. Abu Juhaifa said he was present when the Prophet addressed a man beside him with this instruction.

Khalid bin al-Walid reported that roasted desert lizard was brought to the Prophet. He reached for it, but was told what it was and withdrew his hand. Khalid asked if it was unlawful. The Prophet said, No, but it is not found in my people's land, so I am not inclined to eat it. Khalid ate while the Messenger watched. Malik's version from Ibn Shihab describes it as a roasted lizard.

Itban bin Malik, who had attended Badr among the Ansar, came to the Messenger of Allah and said, My eyesight has weakened, and I lead my people in prayer. When rain comes, the valley between us flows, and I cannot reach their mosque. I would like you to come and pray in my house so I can make that place a prayer area. He said, I will do so, if Allah wills. The next morning, after the sun had risen, the Messenger of Allah came with Abu Bakr and asked permission to enter. He did not sit down before entering the house, then asked where Itban wanted him to pray. Itban pointed to a place. The Prophet stood, said Allahu akbar, and they lined up behind him. He prayed two units, gave the greeting of peace, and they kept him to eat a dish of barley-and-meat soup they had prepared. Some men from the household gathered. Someone asked where Malik bin al-Dukhshun was, and another called him a hypocrite who did not love Allah and His Messenger. The Prophet said, Do not say that. Do you not see that he says, There is no god but Allah, seeking Allah's face? They said Allah and His Messenger knew best, and that they saw him associating with and advising the hypocrites. The Prophet said, Allah has forbidden the Fire for whoever says, There is no god but Allah, seeking Allah's face. Ibn Shihab later asked al-Husayn bin Muhammad al-Ansari, one of the leading men of Banu Salim, about Mahmuds account, and he confirmed it.

Ibn Abbas said that his aunt gave the Prophet desert lizards, dried curds, and milk. The lizards were placed on his dining cloth; had they been unlawful, they would not have been placed there. He drank the milk and ate the dried curds.

Sahl bin Sad said, We used to look forward to Friday. An elderly woman would take beetroot stalks and cook them in a pot with some barley grains. After we prayed, we would visit her, and she would serve it to us. We were happy for Friday because of this. We would not have lunch or take a midday rest until after Friday prayer. By Allah, it had no fat or melted animal fat in it.

Ibn Abbas reported that the Messenger of Allah ate meat from a shoulder, then stood and prayed without performing ablution. Ibn Abbas reported the Prophet's action: after eating meat from a shoulder, he stood and performed the prayer.
Ibn Abbas reported that the Prophet took a piece of meat from a pot and ate it, then prayed without performing ablution.

Abdullah bin Abi Qatadah reported from his father: We went out with the Prophet in the direction of Mecca. The narrator Abdullah bin Abi Qatadah related this from his father, who was among those accompanying the Prophet on the journey.

Abu Qatadah said: One day I was sitting with some Companions of the Prophet at a house on the road to Mecca. The Messenger of Allah had stopped ahead of us. The others were in the state of ihram, while I was not. They saw a wild donkey while I was busy repairing my sandal. They did not tell me about it, though they wished I had seen it. I turned and saw it, saddled my horse, mounted, and pursued the donkey. I had forgotten my whip and spear, so I asked them to hand them to me. They swore they would not help me hunt it. I was angry, dismounted, took them, mounted again, chased the donkey, and brought it down. It died, and the others ate from it. Then they worried whether they could eat it while in ihram. On our way back I kept a shoulder with me. We caught up with the Messenger of Allah and asked him about it. He asked whether we had any of it left. I handed him the shoulder, and he ate from it, stripping the meat from the bone, while he was in ihram. Ibn Jafar also reported the same account from Zayd bin Aslam, from Ata bin Yasar, from Abu Qatadah.

Amr bin Umayyah reported that he saw the Prophet cutting meat from a sheep's shoulder with a knife in his hand. He was called to prayer, so he put down the meat and the knife, stood, and prayed without performing ablution. The report came from Amr bin Umayyah through his son Jafar. It describes what the Prophet did when the call to prayer came while he was cutting the meat.
Abu Huraira said, The Prophet never found fault with food. If he liked it, he ate it; if he disliked it, he left it. Abu Huraira reported this description of the Prophet's manners at meals.
Sahl was asked whether they had ever eaten fine sifted flour in the time of the Prophet. He said no. He was asked whether they sifted barley, and he said no, but they blew away its husks.

Abu Huraira said that one day the Prophet distributed dates among his Companions, giving each person seven. He gave me seven too, one of which was shriveled and poor in quality. Yet none of the dates pleased me more, because it stuck between my teeth as I chewed it.

Sad said, I saw myself as one of seven people with the Prophet. We had nothing to eat except leaves from a climbing plant, until our droppings resembled those of sheep. Then Banu Asad came to admonish me about Islam. I would have been lost and my efforts wasted, then.

Sahl bin Sad was asked whether the Messenger of Allah ate finely sifted flour. He said the Messenger never saw such flour from the time Allah sent him until He took him. Sahl was asked whether they had sieves then, and said the Messenger never saw a sieve either. He was asked how they ate unsifted barley. He said they ground it, blew away what flew off, moistened what remained, and ate it. Sahl explained that they ground the barley, blew away the chaff, moistened what remained, and then ate it. He also said the Prophet never saw a sieve during his lifetime.

Abu Huraira passed by some people with a roasted sheep before them. They invited him to eat, but he refused and said, The Messenger of Allah left this world without ever eating his fill of barley bread. Abu Huraira declined the invitation and explained that the Messenger of Allah had never eaten his fill of barley bread during his life.
Anas said the Prophet never ate at a raised table, from a small individual dish, or finely baked thin bread. I asked Qatadah what they ate from, and he replied, From cloths spread on the ground.
Aishah said that from the time the family of Muhammad arrived in Medina until the Prophet passed away, they never ate their fill of wheat bread for three nights in a row.

Aishah used to order talbina porridge to be cooked when someone in her family died and women gathered to mourn. She would have bread porridge prepared, pour the talbina over it, and say, Eat it, for I heard the Messenger of Allah say, Talbina comforts the heart of the sick person and relieves some of his grief. Aishah shared this practice and the Prophet's teaching about the comforting effect of the porridge.

Abu Musa al-Ashari reported that the Prophet said, Many men attained perfection, but among women only Maryam daughter of Imran and Asiyah, Pharaoh's wife, attained it. Aishah's superiority over other women is like the superiority of tharid, a dish of bread and broth, over all other foods.
